scenario.name: Microsoft SQL Server Security, Mandiant & MITRE T1505.001 — MSSQL Linked Server RPC, xp_cmdshell & Unsafe CLR Assembly Forensics
scenario.overview: Imagine a quiet city public library with towering mahogany bookshelves packed with colorful books, green banker lamps on reading tables, a checkout desk, and a locked rare-book cage. Inside the calm public library reading hall, a visitor pulls an index card from the wooden catalog drawer and alters the shelf call-number to point into the staff archive. In this real-world scenario, the intruder moves quietly past the library check-out desk into neighboring restricted rooms, then smuggles copied records out past the library check-out desk in tiny disguised batches. When the head librarian audits the evening circulation ledger, a restricted rare-book call number checked out on a regular visitor card immediately raises the alarm. In this scenario (T1021, Microsoft SQL Server Security, Mandiant & MITRE T1505.001, MSSQL Linked Server RPC, xp_cmdshell & Unsafe CLR Assembly Forensics), the attacker follows one continuous intrusion path so each later Step can show the exact handoff that makes the next stage possible. The attack unfolds in one continuous arc: mSSQL Linked Server Enumeration, then configuration Change Enabling xp_cmdshell, then in-Memory Hexadecimal CLR Assembly. Steps #1–#3 walk that chain end-to-end by covering MSSQL Linked Server Enumeration, then Configuration Change Enabling xp_cmdshell, then In-Memory Hexadecimal CLR Assembly, while the Process Hierarchy tab keeps the Parent → Child spawn tree visible so you can see which trusted process launched the next payload. Primary detection pivots on SIEM Event 33205 correlated across the documented kill chain.

steps.simpleExplanation: To persist custom .NET stored procedures without dropping a .dll file to the Windows filesystem, the attacker executes CREATE ASSEMBLY FROM 0x4D5A... WITH PERMISSION_SET = UNSAFE, storing the compiled PE bytes directly inside sys.assembly_files (logged in WinEvent Event 33205 with CatalogTable=sys.assemblies / sys.assembly_files, AssemblyName=SqlDiagnosticExt, PermissionSet=UNSAFE_ACCESS , Full OS & Network Access inside sqlservr.exe so analysts can verify the exact actor and target artifact).
